question: Should OpenClaw reject unsafe byte-size config values above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER during validation, even when an existing bad config previously rounded and continued?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and consistent with duration parsing, but stricter config validation can intentionally stop an existing setup that contains an unsafe byte-size value.

options.title: Accept fail-fast validation
options.body: Merge the PR as-is because precision-corrupted byte sizes are invalid config and should not keep running silently.

options.title: Require upgrade handling
options.body: Ask for a doctor migration, warning, or documented recovery path before changing validation behavior for existing configs.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-fast validation
recommendation.body: Merge the PR as-is because precision-corrupted byte sizes are invalid config and should not keep running silently.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is tied to the safe-duration precedent and shared byte-size config parser history.
